alt: 曾被同學撕毀畫作的孩子，看見對方的本子掉進泥水，仍溫和地送上乾淨備用本，對方羞愧又感激地接過。
scene_prompt: 以德報怨 means responding with kindness to someone who previously treated you badly, not simply helping a friend. ONE coherent contemporary school courtyard scene, TWO older children. A boy in a green shirt calmly offers his own clean spare sketchbook to a remorseful boy in an orange shirt whose current sketchbook has just fallen into a muddy puddle at his feet. Green-shirt boy's own torn pencil drawing lies visibly on the nearby bench, and a small pale pencil memory vignette above them clearly shows the orange-shirt boy earlier deliberately tearing that same green-shirt boy's flower drawing, while green-shirt boy looked hurt. The main present-day act must dominate the page: the previously hurt child smiling gently and offering kindness anyway, the former bully ashamed and gratefully receiving. Use only one small soft-edged memory bubble with exactly these same two children, no arrows or words. Clear visual cause-and-response, no violence, no injury. Anatomically correct natural arms and hands; each present-day child two arms and two legs; realistic hand-to-book contact. Warm graphite and watercolor paper texture; no writing on drawings, no text.
